page.layout: Two printed areas on this scan. Left, at the gutter edge: a narrow strip of the facing left page, its outer line ends, cut short by the binding. Right, the printed page: running head centred at top, page number at top right, a centred chapter heading with its subtitle, then a tree diagram of braces and boxes at left and centre, with running text starting at the foot.; One printed page, central text column with a bracketed diagram fragment at the top; a narrow fragment of margin text at the left edge of the scan, and a small signature at the foot of the text. Left-side margin fragments: "untur", "de dis", "o quas", "ntes", "preq", "r: sed", "poteft", "Hinc", "PVI" (fragmentary, partly cut off).

page.notes: The diagram's right-hand labels are partly cut at the image edge; the word "Diuisio" and the start of "Simplex" continue beyond the visible part. Left-edge fragments belong to the facing page and are cut by the gutter. Several lines are only partly legible. The page is a fragment, with the left margin cut off. The large initial N is a woodcut letter joined to "OTATIO" as "NOTATIO". Greek "Ἀπαιϑμησις" is printed as shown, with some doubt on its exact letters. The left-edge margin fragments are cut and only partly legible, so they are not transcribed as notes. The signature "B 4" appears at the foot, with "gici" at the line end, possibly a catchword-like continuation of "Logici".
